tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session demonstrates navigating to the Magento admin Categories page, closing an Incoming Message popup, selecting a category, opening Add Subcategory/Add Root Category dialogs, filling the Name and other fields, and saving. The tool will automate the common flow: open the categories page, close blocking popup, choose the correct Add flow (root vs sub) based on a parent_category parameter, fill required fields (Name, Is Active, Include in Navigation Menu, Store View) and save.

Task Definition:
- Single purpose: create a category in Magento 1.x admin. If parent_category is an empty string the tool will create a root category; otherwise it creates a subcategory under the named parent.

Action Plan (ordered):
1) Navigate to the provided admin categories URL.
2) Wait a moment for initial scripts and overlays.
3) Close the Incoming Message popup if present (click 'close').
4) Agentic decision: If parent_category=='' click Add Root Category; otherwise select the parent node (XPath by visible text) and click Add Subcategory. The agent step is necessary because the tree selection and add-button combination is dynamic and depends on the presence/visibility of elements. This avoids brittle branching in pure deterministic steps.
5) Wait for the Add form to load.
6) Input category_name into the Name input (input#name or input[name='name']).
7) Set Is Active via select[name='is_active'].
8) Set Include in Navigation Menu via select[name='include_in_menu'].
9) Set Store View via select[name='store'] (or the store switcher select id).
10) Click Save Category (toolbar button/title 'Save Category').
11) Wait for saving to complete.
12) Extract page content (success message and tree text) to confirm the creation and return a stable identifier.

Variable Identification (inputs required):
- admin_url (string, required): the categories page URL used for navigation.
- parent_category (string, required): visible parent tree text; empty string means create root.
- category_name (string, required): the new category Name (required by Magento form).
- is_active (string, required): 'Yes'/'No' or '1'/'0'. Magento expects yes/no values; tool passes visible text to the select.
- include_in_menu (string, required): 'Yes'/'No' or '1'/'0'. Required for creation.
- store_view (string, required): Which store view to set (choose 'All Store Views' when in doubt).

Step Optimization and Rationale:
- Use a navigation step to open the categories page instead of replicating menu clicks.
- Prefer visible-text XPaths for tree nodes (starts-with / contains) because counts in parentheses are dynamic. For example (//a[starts-with(normalize-space(.),'{parent_category}')])[1].
- Use an agent step to decide which 'Add' action to perform; the tree selection and 'Add Subcategory' vs 'Add Root Category' logic is dynamic and benefits from agentic reasoning rather than brittle deterministic selectors. This also addresses earlier test failures related to selector ambiguity by letting the agent examine the live DOM and use the best available element.
- Use name/id-based selectors for form fields wherever possible (input#name, select[name='include_in_menu'], select[name='is_active'], select[name='store']). These are stable across Magento 1.x installs.
- Provide multiple selector fallbacks for Save (title-based, class-based, id-based) to avoid 'locator resolved to multiple elements' kind of failures.

Important constraints and notes:
- The agent is expected to already be authenticated (the recorded session was logged in). This tool does not perform login; provide an admin_url reachable within an authenticated session.
- The tool avoids optional exploratory steps: it only performs the essential actions required to create the category and confirm the save.
- The tool uses an agent step to handle dynamic, DOM-dependent choices (selecting the parent node then clicking Add Subcategory vs clicking Add Root Category). This reduces flakiness and respects the developer instruction to actually interact when recording selectors.

Selectors and timing improvements to address past failures:
- Use XPath that does not rely on the numeric counts in node text. Example: (//a[starts-with(normalize-space(.),'{parent_category}')])[1].
- Close the 'Incoming Message' popup by anchor text 'close' before interacting with the tree; recorded element hash was observed but XPath by visible text is used in the deterministic click step to keep the tool portable.
- Wait steps inserted after actions that typically trigger the loading mask. The tool also waits after Save to allow the server-side save to complete and any overlay to disappear before extracting verification info.

This tool targets Magento 1.x admin patterns (names/ids: name, include_in_menu, is_active, store). If a given installation uses different field names or a heavily customized admin theme the agent step will attempt to use visible labels and fallbacks to find the correct controls.
name: magento_admin_create_category
description: Create or update a Magento category (create a root category or create a subcategory under an existing category) in the Magento 1.x Admin Categories screen. Steps: open categories page, dismiss common blocking popup, choose Add Root or Add Subcategory (agent step uses {parent_category} to decide), fill required fields (Name, Is Active, Include in Navigation Menu, Store View) and save. Finally extract page content to confirm save and return the created/updated node text.

steps.description: Open the Magento admin Categories management page (starting point).
Allow initial page scripts and overlays to settle (short wait for loading mask to appear/disappear).
If present, close the 'Incoming Message' popup by clicking its 'close' link. XPath targets the visible 'close' anchor.
Brief pause after closing any popup so the UI can settle.
Agentic step to choose Add Root vs Add Subcategory and perform the appropriate clicks (handles dynamic DOM/tree).
steps.task: Decide which 'Add' flow to trigger based on the parameter {parent_category}. If {parent_category} is the empty string '' then click the 'Add Root Category' control (XPath: //a[normalize-space(.)='Add Root Category'] | //button[normalize-space(.)='Add Root Category']). Otherwise: locate the parent node in the left category tree by visible text (robust XPath: (//a[starts-with(normalize-space(.),'{parent_category}')])[1]) and click it to select the parent, wait for the category edit UI to load, then click the 'Add Subcategory' control (XPath: //a[normalize-space(.)='Add Subcategory'] | //button[normalize-space(.)='Add Subcategory']). After performing the click(s) return control. Use up to 6 internal steps to find and click elements, waiting for common loaders (#loading-mask or ajax loader gifs) to disappear between actions.

steps.description: Wait for the Add form to open and any loaders to clear.
Fill the Name field for the new category. Uses input#name or input[name='name'] (common Magento attributes).
Set 'Is Active' (Yes/No). Targets select[name='is_active'] as used in Magento admin forms.
Set 'Include in Navigation Menu' (Yes/No). Targets select[name='include_in_menu'] which is the standard Magento field name.
Set the Store View selector. The step targets common store-switcher select names/ids and chooses the requested store view.
Click the top toolbar 'Save Category' button. Uses title-based and common class/id fallbacks.
steps.cssSelector: button[title='Save Category'], button.save, button#save, input[title='Save Category']

steps.description: Wait for the save operation to complete and for any loading mask to disappear.
Collect page messages (e.g., 'The category has been saved.') and the left-tree text to verify creation and obtain the final visible node text for the new/updated category.
steps.goal: Confirm that the category has been created or updated; capture any success messages and the left tree text for the created category to provide a stable identifier.

input_schema.name: admin_url
input_schema.description: Full URL for Magento admin Categories page (example: 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_category/'). The tool will navigate to this URL as the first step.

input_schema.name: parent_category
input_schema.description: Visible text of the parent category to create the new category under. If you want to create a root category instead, pass the empty string ''. Use the visible tree text (for example 'Men' or 'Default Category').

input_schema.name: category_name
input_schema.description: The Name for the new category to create (required). Example: 'Bot Subcategory Automated by Tool 2026' or 'Tool Root Category Created by Bot 2026'.

input_schema.name: is_active
input_schema.description: Set the 'Is Active' field for the category. Common values: 'Yes' or 'No' (or '1'/'0').

input_schema.name: include_in_menu
input_schema.description: Set the 'Include in Navigation Menu' field. Use 'Yes' (or '1') to include in navigation.

input_schema.name: store_view
input_schema.description: Store view to use when creating/updating the category. Use the visible option name from the admin (e.g. 'All Store Views', 'English', 'French', 'German').
